newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Montenegrin trade unions protest against poverty.
newsitem.headline: Montenegrin trade unions protest against poverty.

text.p: Under the banner of "Let's go back to jobs -- for dignity of work", some 4,000 Montenegrin trade unionists held a rally here on Thursday.
The rally started at one minute to twelve, symbolising the very last moment for necessary social changes.

"Without foreign investment we can't renew production. The privatisation of the economy is scrapped due to isolation of the country from international financial institutions," the Unions said in a statement.
"The workers are suffering for political reasons," the trade unions said, urging "just and rapid privatisation of the Montenegrin economy".

"We still live in a cage, we demand reintegration into the world community now," the president of the Montenegrin association of trade unions, Danilo Popovic told the workers assembled in the main square.
"Federal officials say that this country is attractive for foreign investments. However, we are regarded as the most risky area for new investments. We are fed up with deceptions," Popovic said.

Montenegro with only 650,000 inhabitants has 25,000 workers who have not been paid for over three months, 20,000 on compulsory leave. Some 10,000 have been dismissed and further burdening its economy are 78,000 pensioners, the union says.
The 65,000 unemployed workers are expected to be joined by 25,000 more. The 125,000 people in work receive on average less than 190 German marks a month.

"This is just a beginning. This is the first time that the Montenegrin trade unions have organised such a rally and we are happy with today's worker support. If the government does not meet our demands in three months we will ask for extraordinary elections," Popovic told Reuters after the rally.
Yugoslavia, comprising Serbia and Montenegro, has been suspended from membership of international financial institutions.

The suspension is expected to remain until Belgrade cooperates with a war crimes tribunal, shows commitment to democracy and improves its human rights record, especialy in Serbia's mostly-Albanian province of Kosovo.

Demands from Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic that Belgrade meets these demands have been met with hostility in Belgrade and caused a rift between his reformist forces and hardliners of Montenegro's President Momir Bulatovic.
